title: Agents in the release pipeline: generating a change is not authorizing it

source.title: Digital.ai — Release 26.3 brings AI agents into governed enterprise delivery

summary: Digital.ai Release 26.3 puts agents inside software-delivery workflows. My take: the release boundary matters, and authorization has to hold across every entry point, including MCP, retries, and delegation.

title: Agent memory should be judged by behavior, not recall

source.title: RAG in a Trenchcoat: When Minimal Memory Is Enough for Agentic Systems, and When It Isn't (arXiv)

summary: A simple memory system, BRIDGE, holds up against more complex designs, but retrieving a rule doesn't mean the model applies it. Memory should be evaluated in three stages: preserved, retrieved, and applied.

title: When the right correction never reaches the user

source.title: RagHarnessDebugger: Jev-Guided Agentic RAG in Contract Inference Repair Auditing (arXiv)

summary: An agentic RAG system can find the evidence and generate the fix, then have its own acceptance rules block it. Final accuracy hides this; corrections and regressions need to be measured separately.

title: MCP Discovery Hub: finding a tool is not the same as trusting it

source.title: SnapLogic — MCP Discovery Hub and new AI agent building and governance capabilities

summary: SnapLogic launched a searchable catalog of MCP servers and tools. A catalog helps build an inventory, but trust still needs ownership, versioning, revocation, and authorization checks when tools are called.

title: When repositories try to instruct your AI coding assistant

source.title: Bitdefender Labs — How AI agents become new targets in a GitHub malware campaign

summary: Bitdefender found 22 malicious GitHub links aimed at AI-assisted development. Instructions inside a repository should never be trusted automatically; understanding them must be paired with limits on executing them.

title: Microsoft's AI Transparency Initiative: verify what agents did, not just what they say

source.title: Microsoft — AI Transparency Initiative to strengthen enterprise trust in AI models and agents

summary: Microsoft and 40+ organizations announced a shared approach to AI transparency. I agree with independent verification; the real test is whether the evidence can detect problems, enforce limits, and reconstruct events.

title: Agentic threats are here: the urgency depends on what AI can reach

source.title: Google Threat Intelligence Group — Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold

summary: Google and Mandiant report attackers using agentic systems to run parts of cyber operations. My take: judge urgency by access, autonomy, scale, and consequences, and make sure a model's decision can never grant itself more permission.

title: The building blocks: Transformers, RAG, agents, multi-agent systems, agentic architectures, and MCP

source.title: Foundational reading: Attention Is All You Need, the RAG paper, Building Effective Agents, and the MCP docs

summary: Six related terms that describe different parts of an AI system, explained through one familiar example: an AI shopping assistant helping someone choose a laptop.
